title: Trapping Rain Water
strengths: Derived the per-index water formula using the smaller of the left and right boundaries.
Correctly identified the O(n^2) repeated scanning in the brute-force solution.
Recognized that storing heights is sufficient; boundary indices are unnecessary.
Implemented a correct O(n) time, O(1) extra-space two-pointer solution.
weaknesses: Needed guidance to identify the smaller boundary as the decisive constraint.
Needed substantial guidance to move from prefix/suffix maxima to the O(1)-space two-pointer invariant.
Initially considered an unnecessary additional index.
The first array implementation still rescanned both sides and remained O(n^2).
selection_reason: Previously selected as one of two Hard problems in the weekly random Top Interview 150 set; the pattern was hidden until completion.
recognition_signals: The answer at each position depends on constraints from both directions.
The smaller of two boundaries limits the result.
A straightforward solution repeatedly recomputes left/right information.
One side can be finalized without knowing the exact future state of the other side.

learning_reflection.concern: Recognized two pointers, but initially considered adding another index. Reaching the simpler solution took a long time, and identifying the smaller boundary as the key constraint was difficult.
analysis: The main difficulty was minimizing state after recognizing two pointers.
Before adding another index, ask whether an existing pointer can serve the same role.
When several values constrain an answer, identify the bottleneck.
Ask whether exact information from both sides is actually necessary.
learning_reflection.transfer_question: Which position can I finalize using only the information I currently have?

rewrites.original: The shorter side decides the water level.
rewrites.improved: The water level is limited by the shorter of the two boundaries.

rewrites.original: Finding highest left and right bar is repeated.
rewrites.improved: We repeatedly recompute the maximum height on the left and right for neighboring positions.

rewrites.original: time complexity is O(n) since we scan at once using two pointer. and O(1) time complexity.
rewrites.improved: The time complexity is O(n) because each pointer moves inward at most n times in total, and the extra space complexity is O(1).
